title: Effects and mechanisms of prenatal microplastics exposure on glucose metabolic function in male rat offspring
content:
Abstract
In recent years, microplastics have emerged as significant environmental pollutants with potential detrimental effects on fetal development. This study aimed to examine the effects of prenatal exposure to polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) on glucose metabolic function in adult male offspring rats and to elucidate the role of the pancreatic and duodenal homeobox 1 (PDX-1) gene in this rocess. Methods: From gestational day 10 until delivery, the pregnant rats were orally gavaged with low dose (1 mg/kg·d) and high dose (10 mg/kg·d) microplastics, respectively. The intrauterine development of the offspring was assessed and adult male offspring subsequently underwent an intraperitoneal glucose tolerance test and an insulin tolerance test. We conducted morphological analysis of pancreatic tissue, along with analysis of PDX-1 expression and epigenetic changes in its promoter region in pancreatic tissue. We found that prenatal PS-MPs sexposure resulted in a significant decrease in neonatal birth weight and an increased incidence of intrauterine growth restriction. The exposed groups exhibited impaired pancreatic development, evidenced by reduced Blood glucose and insulin levels. Adult male offspring displayed diabetic phenotypes characterized by elevated fasting blood glucose levels and impaired glucose tolerance, with significant morphological alterations in the pancreas. Mechanistic analyses revealed decreased PDX-1 expression associated with altered epigenetic marks in its promoter region. These findings suggest that prenatal PS-MPs exposure can lead to inhibition of glucose metabolism in adult male offspring rats, which may be related to the inhibition of β-cell proliferation caused by changes in epigenetic modifications in the PDX-1 gene promoter region of pancreatic tissue.
